items.question: What practice, after six months, frees the ochre-robed practitioner from bondage and disease and unites him with yogis?
premises: Six months of practice frees from bondage.
The practitioner wears an ochre robe.
Freedom from bondage precedes yogic union.
items.inference: The verse prescribes six-month practice leading to liberation and union with yogis.
uncertainties: Exact gender of kāṣāyaṃ is inferred from context.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months, wearing an ochre robe free from bondage, becomes free from all diseases and joins the yogis in union; this practice of the soul has been told to you, O Bhairavi.

items.question: What practice, after six months, frees the ochre-robed practitioner from bondage and disease and unites him with yogis?
premises: Freedom from all diseases is attained.
The union is together with them.
items.inference: The verse states the practitioner becomes disease-free and joins yogis in union.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of saha+melakam is inferred.

items.question: What practice, after six months, frees the ochre-robed practitioner from bondage and disease and unites him with yogis?
